region: Modelling: training, scoring, explainability, MLflow IO
purpose: Owns the model lifecycle for the pricing engine: (1) training jobs (CatBoost gradient boosting + RustyStats GLM) orchestrated as a memory-bounded, cancellable, parquet-staged pipeline (prepare -> split -> fit -> evaluate/diagnostics -> save artifact + feature contract -> optional MLflow log); (2) a uniform ScoringModel interface with explicit per-flavor dispatch (catboost/pyfunc/rustystats) and automatic feature-type casting at predict time; (3) per-prediction SHAP/contribution explainability with additivity self-checks for trace enrichment; (4) MLflow persistence (logging with ModelSignature, thread-safe in-memory + on-disk model load cache, artifact discovery); (5) the train-to-deploy feature contract that pins feature schema and categorical domains so train/score drift fails loudly.
public_surface: modelling.TrainingJob / TrainResult (run(progress, on_iteration, check_cancelled, execution_context) -> TrainResult)
modelling.log_experiment / MLflowLogResult; resolve_tracking_backend / resolve_experiment_name / configure_mlflow_tracking / build_run_url

_mlflow_io.load_mlflow_model / load_local_model / ScoringModel / clear_model_cache / get_model_cache_stats; shared scoring helpers _score_eager, _prepare_predict_frame, _append_classification_proba, _positive_class_proba_vector
depends_on: haute._types (PipelineGraph, GraphNode, NodeType, _Frame) — foundational graph model
haute.execution / _execute_lazy (execute_lazy_graph, build_dataframe_execution_cache_request, dataframe_graph_input_fingerprint, AllExceptColumns, reuse_loaded_model_by_node wiring)
haute._execution_context / _execution_admission (ExecutionContext, ExecutionProfile, admission, memory ceiling, cancellation token)
haute._hashing (content_hash_bytes / xxh64); haute._ram_estimate (available_ram_bytes, estimate_safe_training_rows, GPU VRAM estimate)
External: catboost, rustystats (optional), mlflow, polars, pyarrow, numpy
depended_on_by: haute.executor / _builders / _codegen_builders — MODEL_SCORE node execution + script generation
haute.deploy._scorer / _bundler — deploy-time scoring and artifact bundling (load_local_model, feature contract, score_frame via _run_score_pipeline)
haute.chunking / execution — chunked streaming scoring with reuse_loaded_model
frontend (modelling config panel, training diagnostics charts) via TrainResponse schema
internal_dataflow: TRAIN (in): HTTP TrainRequest -> TrainService.start validates config, merges declared categorical_levels from upstream nodes, estimates safe RAM rows + GPU VRAM, executes the upstream lazy graph and bounded_sink to a temp parquet (column-projected to features+target+weight+offset+id), then TrainingJob.run reads that parquet. TrainingJob: _prepare_data (validate schema from parquet metadata, count+filter null targets into a clean temp parquet, derive features=all-cols minus {target,weight,offset,fold,id,exclude,split-cols}, snapshot feature/target dtypes + categorical_levels) -> _split_data (split_mask 0/1/2 written as _partition column via bounded_sink) -> _train_model (read partitions via streaming_collect, build CatBoost Pool with float32 cast / pandas only when categoricals present, or pass DataFrame to GLM) -> _compute_metrics (read diagnostics partition once: holdout>validation>train, compute metrics+SHAP+PDP+Lorenz+AvE, optional diagnostics recorded in diagnostics_errors) -> _save_artifacts (native .cbm/.rsglm + per-model {name}.feature_contract.json) -> _log_to_mlflow. TRAIN (out): TrainResult -> TrainResponse (JSON, asserted finite) via JobLifecycle; model file + contract on disk; MLflow run with ModelSignature, JSON diagnostics artifacts, model card. SCORE (in): MODEL_SCORE node config (run_id/artifact or registered model) -> ModelScorer / score_from_config -> load_mlflow_model (cache lookup -> disk cache -> download+atomic-move -> wrap as ScoringModel) -> _run_score_pipeline: _validate_features(model vs schema, memoised) -> optional categorical-domain validation on the single materialisation -> score_frame (explicit flavor dispatch -> _prepare_predict_frame casts per flavor) -> eager predict OR batched sink->iter_batches->predict->parquet -> optional user post-processing code -> projected LazyFrame. EXPLAIN (in): config + input_row + traced prediction -> load model -> build one-row Pool/frame -> SHAP/contributions with raw-vs-response additivity check -> ranked contribution dict (out) for trace UI.
concurrency_model: Training: at most one training job at a time (TrainService._check_no_concurrent_jobs under _start_lock against JobStore status); each job runs the pipeline on a daemon thread; cancellation is cooperative via CancellableJobRegistry + ExecutionContext.checkpoint() polled from _report/_on_iteration/check_cancelled; CatBoost GPU fit runs on a worker thread polling learn_error.tsv with a bounded abort-join (30s) and loud zombie logging. Model load cache (_mlflow_io._model_cache, _ModelCacheWithCascade over LRUCache, max 16): per-(run_id, artifact_path) reentrant I/O lock (WeakValueDictionary) provides single-flight download+load (avoids thundering herd, rename-over-open-file, and corrupt-retry-unlink races); disk-cache eviction guarded by a per-run in-use Counter so an active run dir is never rmtree'd; eviction cascades to invalidate _model_scorer feature-validation cache (also LRU max 16) outside the cache lock to avoid deadlock. Cache hit/miss counters under a dedicated stats lock. Feature-validation cache adds a non-locked single-entry last-entry fast path keyed on id(model)+contract+schema items. Deploy + contract caches are StatGatedCache (per-key single-flight, gated on mtime_ns+size). ScoringModel reuse pinned per-scorer under a lock for streaming chunk jobs. Temp-file cleanup uses a module lock + atexit + contextvar scope.
perf_characteristics: Designed for low peak memory on wide/large data: parquet staging at every stage with streaming bounded_sink, column projection pushed into scans (GLM reads only term cols; CatBoost reads features+target+weight+offset), float32 cast for CatBoost Pools, aggressive del+gc.collect()+_malloc_trim between stages, and a persistent RSS memory log (_mem_checkpoint). Scoring offers eager (single predict, one materialisation) vs batched (sink + 500k-row parquet iter_batches) paths chosen by caller, never auto-detected. Model loads cached in-memory (16) and on-disk (.cache/models, 50 run dirs, atomic move, ~30s+ saved vs Databricks re-download). Feature validation, contract reads, and deploy artifacts memoised on hot per-request/per-batch paths. Diagnostics partition read exactly once. SHAP subsamples to 1000 rows. Known cost: explainability and per-batch validation re-derive categorical sets; batched scoring writes a full intermediate parquet.
invariants: Cache key uniquely identifies model content: _model_cache_key=(source_type, resolved_run_id, version_or_artifact, task); a wrong key returns the wrong model. The fast-path key (version='') must agree with the resolved-path key for the same artifact.

Feature order is positional for CatBoost: categorical indices are positional, so _validate_features enforces the input schema presents model features in the SAME relative order as training; a reorder must raise, never silently mis-encode.

Per-flavor predict-frame contract: rustystats gets raw Polars, pyfunc gets named pandas with native dtypes (no preemptive float downcast), catboost gets float32 numerics + _MISSING_-filled pd.Categorical; unknown flavor must raise, never fall through to catboost/pyfunc shape.

Eager and batched scoring must produce identical predictions and identical proba semantics — both route shape reduction through _positive_class_proba_vector (1-D as-is, (n,1)->col0, (n,2)->col1, multiclass raises).

Row alignment is structural: eager scoring collects ONCE and attaches predictions to that same frame so an order-unstable upstream (group_by w/o maintain_order, unique, streaming join) cannot land predictions on wrong rows; categorical-domain validation runs on the same materialisation that is scored.

Feature contract hash = sha256 of canonical sort-keyed JSON of all fields except the hash; load_contract must reject a hash that disagrees with content. categorical_levels are explicit metadata, never inferred from rows; None is an explicit null level.

Train-vs-score drift fails loudly: assert_contracts_match raises FeatureMismatchError naming the offending field; deploy _assert_runtime_contract_matches rebuilds the contract from live schema before any model load.
Null-target rows must be removed before any trainer sees them; a temporal split with null dates must raise (no silent routing); split fractions validation_size+holdout_size<1.

Artifact disk-cache path never escapes cache_root: _validate_disk_cache_run_id + _validate_artifact_path + is_relative_to(cache_root) guard; run_id/artifact_path with sep/..\/NUL must raise. score_from_config config path must resolve within project root.

SHAP/contribution explanations must reconstruct the model prediction within tolerance (raw-formula space for CatBoost, accounting for Poisson/Tweedie exp link); a mismatch raises rather than presenting a wrong attribution. GLM inference stats are never fabricated (GLMInferenceUnavailableError).

config->TrainingJob kwargs is single-sourced (build_train_params/build_training_job_kwargs) so live training and exported scripts can never train different models; GLM keys merged for GLM only (CatBoost has no **kwargs).
Run-owned temp parquets (owns_tmp=True) are always cleaned on abort; caller-supplied parquet inputs are never deleted.
Optional diagnostics (SHAP/PDP/GLM) failures are recorded in diagnostics_errors and surfaced, never silently swallowed; mandatory steps (feature_importance, compute_metrics) propagate.

candidate_risks.concern: pyfunc/RustyStats models are logged with loader_module="haute._mlflow_io" (_mlflow_log.py:471-475) but _mlflow_io defines no module-level _load_pyfunc(path)/load_model symbol that MLflow's pyfunc loader-module contract requires (only _load_pyfunc_model(mlflow, run_id, artifact_path), a different signature). A consumer loading the logged model through mlflow.pyfunc.load_model(runs:/.../model) would hit AttributeError/contract failure; haute only works because it separately logs the native .rsglm via mlflow.log_artifact and loads that instead.
candidate_risks.why: Silent contract breakage: the MLflow artifact advertises a pyfunc flavor that cannot actually be loaded by standard MLflow tooling, and the ModelSignature attached to it is the documented drift-detection surface for deploy. External consumers or future code paths relying on pyfunc.load_model would fail or be misled.
candidate_risks.why_severity: Hidden until someone loads via the pyfunc flavor; native path masks it for the common case.

candidate_risks.concern: load_mlflow_model fast-path uses cache key with version='' for source_type=='run' (artifact known), while the resolved path builds the key with resolved_version. For source_type=='run' resolved_version stays '' so they match, but if a run-sourced load ever resolves a non-empty version, the fast-path PUT (version='') and the resolved GET (version set) would diverge and double-load / never hit. Also _model_cache is keyed by raw run_id on the fast path but resolved_run_id elsewhere; for 'run' these are equal, but registered models only ever take the slow path.
candidate_risks.why: Cache-key divergence silently defeats the cache (extra downloads) or, worse, could serve a stale entry if a run_id maps to different artifacts across versions. Numerical correctness is fine but performance/observability invariants degrade invisibly.
candidate_risks.why_severity: Current call paths keep the keys consistent; risk is latent if version semantics for run sources change.

candidate_risks.concern: CatBoostAlgorithm.predict (used for TRAINING-TIME metrics/diagnostics) returns predict_proba[:,1] for a CatBoostClassifier, whereas the SCORING path (ScoringModel.predict via score_frame) returns model.predict() (class label) and appends proba separately. So the y_pred used for training metrics (gini/auc/lorenz/residuals) is the positive-class probability, while scored output 'prediction' is the hard label. Whether this is intended differs by metric; residuals_histogram/actual_vs_predicted on a classification task would mix proba-as-prediction semantics.
candidate_risks.why: Train-time diagnostics and live scoring report different 'prediction' semantics for the same model; a reviewer auditing classification metrics could be misled, and residual-style diagnostics on probabilities vs labels are not obviously correct.
candidate_risks.why_severity: Classification is secondary to the pricing/regression focus, but silent semantic mismatch in reported metrics is a correctness-of-reporting issue.

candidate_risks.concern: _group_split/_group_mask hash groups with md5(seed:group) and take a fraction threshold; this gives no guarantee the realised validation fraction is close to validation_size (it is a Bernoulli draw per group), and the 'force at least one validation group' fallback only triggers when zero groups land in validation. Temporal mask sorts non-train rows by arg_sort of dates that may have ties; holdout assignment via slice of arg_sort is order-dependent on tie-breaking.
candidate_risks.why: Silent statistical bias: a user requesting 20% validation can get a wildly different split with skewed group sizes, affecting reported metrics and model selection without any error. Tie-handling in temporal holdout could be non-deterministic across Polars versions.
candidate_risks.why_severity: Behaviour is deterministic-by-seed and documented as hashing; bias is a known trade-off rather than a bug, but worth a numerical-stability audit.

candidate_risks.concern: _validate_features keys on (id(scoring_model), contract, schema items). id() is reused after an object is GC'd; the design relies on the _model_cache eviction cascade (_invalidate_feature_validation_cache_for) to drop entries when a ScoringModel leaves the cache. But ScoringModels created OUTSIDE _model_cache (e.g. _score_batched_unified builds a transient carrier ScoringModel, load_local_model in deploy, reuse_loaded_model pinned instances) are never registered in _model_cache, so their feature-validation entries are only protected by the contract component of the key against id-reuse — a different model with an identical feature contract and schema but different weights could collide on a reused id and return a stale (usable, missing) tuple.
candidate_risks.why: The cached value is only (usable_features, missing_features), which depends solely on names/contract/schema, so a collision returns a structurally-correct answer; the risk is subtle (entry never validates the NEW object) but currently appears benign because the cached result is content-equivalent. Still a shared-state correctness lead if the cached payload ever grows to include model-specific data.
candidate_risks.why_severity: Cached payload is name/schema-derived so a collision yields the same answer today; flagged because the id()-reuse + selective-cascade design is fragile to future changes.

candidate_risks.concern: GPU CatBoost fit runs on a daemon worker thread; on cancellation the helper joins up to 30s and, if still alive, logs and re-raises leaving train_dir on disk and the thread running. The fit thread holds the CatBoost model and the Pool; abandoning it leaks GPU/host memory and a train_dir, and a subsequent training job is blocked only by the single-job guard at the route layer (the abandoned thread could still be writing files).
candidate_risks.why: Concurrency/resource leak under cancellation: a cancelled GPU run can leave a live writer and temp dir; repeated cancels could accumulate zombie threads/dirs. Loudly logged but not recoverable in-process.
candidate_risks.why_severity: GPU path is opt-in, the abandon is bounded and logged, and the single-job lock limits accumulation; still an unbounded-resource lead under repeated cancellation.

candidate_risks.area: Batched scoring proba in zero-row / projection path
candidate_risks.concern: _batch_score_to_parquet decides can_predict_proba via _raw_model_supports_predict_proba but the empty-frame branch and the per-chunk write_projection branch both gate the proba column on slightly different conditions (want_proba + support vs proba_col present in chunk.columns). If the first batch lacks proba (model returns None at runtime despite advertising predict_proba) but later batches differ, the ParquetWriter schema is fixed from the first table and a later schema change would raise; conversely empty-input writes a Float64 proba column whose presence depends on can_predict_proba, which may not match a non-empty run.
candidate_risks.why: Schema drift between batches / between empty and non-empty inputs could either raise mid-write or produce outputs whose columns depend on row count — a subtle output-contract inconsistency feeding downstream pricing.
candidate_risks.why_severity: Requires a model whose predict_proba support varies at runtime; defensive but a real edge for custom pyfunc models.

candidate_risks.concern: coefficients_table/relativities have multi-level fallbacks (coef_table -> bse/tvalues/pvalues arrays -> raise) and _align_coefs_and_names prepends (Intercept) heuristically when len(coefs)>len(names). If RustyStats ever returns coefficients and names of equal length but mis-ordered, the intercept alignment and the per-index zip in relativities() could silently mislabel coefficients/relativities without tripping the length guard.
candidate_risks.why: Silent mislabeling of GLM relativities (the core actuarial output) would present wrong factor relativities as correct; only length mismatches are guarded, not ordering/identity.
candidate_risks.why_severity: Depends on RustyStats name/coef ordering contract; the explainability path independently re-checks additivity, but the diagnostics table does not.

candidate_risks.concern: _save_artifacts writes a per-model {name}.feature_contract.json but only WARNS (never rewrites/removes) a leftover shared feature_contract.json. If a deploy bundle or a feature_contract_path config still points at the legacy shared file, it silently describes whichever model trained last.
candidate_risks.why: A stale shared contract pointed at by older config silently validates against the wrong model's schema — drift detection would pass when it should fail. Mitigated by per-model naming + loud warning, but the old file is left in place.
candidate_risks.why_severity: Only bites pre-existing deployments using the legacy path; new paths are per-model.

complexity_hotspots.area: load_mlflow_model fast-path vs resolved-path single-flight + disk cache + bounded retry
complexity_hotspots.why: Two cache lookup paths, nested per-artifact locks, disk-cache in-use guard, corrupt-retry with backoff; the highest concentration of concurrency-correctness reasoning in the region.
Multi-stage parquet-staged pipeline with abort-safety nets, null-target cleaning, GLM feature narrowing, read-once diagnostics partition selection, and a long optional-diagnostics block.

complexity_hotspots.area: score_frame / eager+batched unified scoring + write projection + validation cache
complexity_hotspots.why: Unified flavor dispatch, eager vs batched forks, projection column algebra shared across paths, plus the memoised feature-validation cache with last-entry fast path and eviction cascade.
HTTP-to-async lifecycle: admission, RAM/VRAM estimation, lazy graph execution + sink, background thread with extensive per-exception-type state transitions and cleanup.
Raw-formula vs response-space prediction handling, link-function detection, additivity tolerance checks, and contribution ranking/truncation in two parallel implementations.
Numpy index-arithmetic partitioning with date sorting, hash-bucket group assignment, and several edge-case reclassification branches.
GPU/CPU branching, callback vs metric-file progress, worker-thread cancel lifecycle, and post-fit loss-history reconstruction from evals_result_.

test_coverage_observations: Heavy, behaviour-focused coverage across the region: tests/test_model_scorer*.py (contracts, feature projection, eager single execution, feature order lookup), test_mlflow_io*.py (concurrency, real pyfunc, IO), test_model_cache_observability.py, test_lru_cache_contracts.py, test_feature_validation_cache.py, test_cache_unification.py, test_modelling*.py (loud errors, train/score contract, export), test_training_*.py (memory safety, temp cleanup, split streaming, catboost projection, null-target fused split, lorenz nonfinite, job_no_glm_cv, contract_per_model), test_state_transitions.py / test_partial_failure.py (async job lifecycle), test_model_explainability.py, test_glm_integration.py, test_rustystats_algorithm.py, test_train_config_builder.py / test_train_param_routing.py, test_scoring_path_unified.py, test_deploy*.py (scorer artifact cache, contract integrity), plus tests/performance/*. The codebase follows TDD/regression-test discipline (CLAUDE.md). Gaps worth checking later: an explicit test that a logged pyfunc/rsglm model is loadable via mlflow.pyfunc loader_module (the _load_pyfunc symbol gap); classification-task train-metric-vs-scored-prediction semantic equivalence; group/temporal split fraction-balance assertions; GPU cancel zombie-thread/train_dir leak behaviour (hard to test without a GPU).
